immunofluoresence is more sensitive and specific than silver methanamine staining for detection of Pneumocystic carinii in sputum.
immunofluorescent staining using a monoclonal antibody is more specific and more sensitive for the diagnosis of Pneumocystic carinii pneumonia than silver methenamine stain.
immunofluorescent staining with monoclonal antibody to Pneumocystic carinii is more sensitive than silver methanamine staining and is suitable for specimens fixed with ethanol.

the development of new methods of diagnosis of pneumocystosisis.
the detection of Pneumocystosis in patients infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) by the use of monoclonal antibodies (MAb) directed against the parasite.

immunofluorescent staining of bronchoalveola lavage or induced sputum samples using monoclonal antibody is a sensitive and specific test for diagnosing Pneumocystosis.

the diagnosis of pneumocystosis should not be delayed in patients with suspected pneumocystosis and HIV infection, even if the initial bronchoalveoloar lavage is negative for Pneumocystosis.
